assessment_401: Observed behavior (runtime-verified in the packaged leg, not only traced): after the password was rotated, the explorer replayed the stored, dead Authorization header and received 401, keeping the stale value in sessionStorage; the Admin UI's next 401 cleared the stored header and presented the login screen; after re-login the explorer's next request succeeded with the new header. Assessment: this is the pre-existing Admin UI session pattern (the UI interceptor owns session invalidation; the explorer never had a 401 handler), not a regression introduced by this change, whose scope is that the explorer sends the session's current credentials per request. It does not block offering the fix. One disclosure line in the PR is recommended so a reviewer is not surprised. A parity fix (clearing the stored header on an explorer 401) is small but changes shared session semantics and belongs to the PR owner's call.
assessment_disable_js_client: Observed in the adjacent investigation's dry runs: with -PdisableJsClient=true every js-client task leaves the war graph, but the Scalar bundle tasks remain, so a node-less or offline build still runs npm to fetch the 3.5 MB standalone bundle, and no solr/licenses entry covers that bundle. Assessment: this is a build-behavior property of the explorer feature's delivery rather than of the auth fix commit itself. It does not block offering the auth fix. Whether disableJsClient should also drop the explorer page is an intent question for the owner (gating the bundle makes the explorer 404); recommend raising it as a question, not silently changing it.
remaining_gaps: Generated Java, JavaScript and Python clients were verified only to carry the declared '/api' server metadata; behavior behind a path-rewriting reverse proxy was not tested. A split-origin proxy silently stripping Authorization because of the hook's same-origin check is source-grounded, not lab-verified.
JWT login was not exercised; the harness and the packaged setup configure BasicAuth only. Parity is by construction (the same storage key) but unproven at runtime.
The explorer under the new UI was not exercised; all browser evidence is the classic webapp at this head.
Whether the Scalar bundle requires a solr/licenses entry is an open packaging question for the owner, recorded here as unassessed, not as a defect.
